originalTitle: U.S. oil rises above $83 a barrel as Iran says Strait of Hormuz won't open until conditions are met
summary: U.S. oil had risen as much as 3% earlier in the day after President Donald Trump demanded that Iran pay reparations to the U.S.
content:
Oil prices rose Tuesday after a senior Iranian official said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Tehran's conditions are met by Washington.

U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures gained 1.3% to close at $83.20 per barrel. Brent crude , the international benchmark, advanced 1.36% to settle at $88.91 per barrel. Prices have gained more than 6% this week as hopes fade for a deal to increase ship traffic through Hormuz.

The Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, demanded the U.S. unfreeze Iranian funds held overseas as condition for Hormuz to open, according to Reuters.

The oil market was weighing conflicting signals Tuesday about whether the U.S. and Iran were on the verge of a deal.

Pakistan's Defense Minister Khawaja Asif told Bloomberg News that "things are shaping up again in favor of a peace arrangement or a deal." Islamabad mediated the interim U.S.-Iran deal in June that quickly collapsed and led to renewed fighting in Hormuz.

President Donald Trump has escalated his rhetoric this week, demanding that Iran pay reparations to the U.S. One week ago, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that a new deal on Hormuz could come soon, but an agreement still has not materialized.

Ship transits through Hormuz remained very low on Monday with just eight vessels crossing the the strait, according to data from the trade intelligence firm Kpler. More than 130 ships crossed Hormuz before the U.S. and Israel attacked on Feb. 28.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Tuesday that oil exports through Hormuz have reached a seven-day moving average of 9 million barrels per day thanks to the U.S. military. The total oil flows from the Gulf region are averaging around 15 million bpd when pipeline exports are included, Wright said.

Meanwhile, Trump on Monday extended the suspension of a shipping law, the Jones Act, that restricts the transport of goods between American ports to U.S. vessels. He narrowed the waiver to vessels hauling certain energy resources.

Oil stockpiles in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve have fallen below 300 million barrels to the lowest level in more than four decades, according to Deparment of Energy data released Monday. Trump ordered the release of 172 million barrels in March to ease the disruption caused by the Iran war.
chineseTitle: 伊朗称在满足条件之前不会开放霍尔木兹海峡，美国油价升至每桶83美元以上
chineseSummary: 在唐纳德·特朗普总统要求伊朗向美国支付赔偿后，美国石油价格当天早些时候上涨了 3%。
chineseContent:
伊朗高级官员表示，在华盛顿满足德黑兰的条件之前，霍尔木兹海峡不会重新开放，油价周二上涨。

美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨 1.3%，收于每桶 83.20 美元。国际基准布伦特原油上涨 1.36%，收于每桶 88.91 美元。由于达成增加霍尔木兹船舶运输量协议的希望逐渐渺茫，本周价格上涨了 6% 以上。

据路透社报道，伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书穆赫森·雷扎伊要求美国解冻伊朗在海外持有的资金，作为开放霍尔木兹海峡的条件。

周二，石油市场正在权衡美国和伊朗是否即将达成协议的相互矛盾的信号。

巴基斯坦国防部长卡瓦贾·阿西夫告诉彭博新闻社，“局势再次有利于和平安排或达成协议。”伊斯兰堡于 6 月斡旋达成的美伊临时协议很快破裂，并导致霍尔木兹再次爆发战斗。

唐纳德·特朗普总统本周升级了言辞，要求伊朗向美国支付赔款。一周前，财政部长斯科特·贝森特告诉 CNBC，霍尔木兹海峡问题的新协议可能很快就会达成，但协议尚未落实。

根据贸易情报公司 Kpler 的数据，周一通过霍尔木兹海峡的船舶过境量仍然非常低，只有 8 艘船只穿越该海峡。在美国和以色列于 2 月 28 日发动袭击之前，已有 130 多艘船只穿越霍尔木兹海峡。

能源部长克里斯赖特周二表示，由于美国军方的帮助，通过霍尔木兹海峡的石油出口已达到每天 900 万桶的 7 天移动平均水平。 Wright 表示，如果算上管道出口，来自海湾地区的石油流量平均约为每天 1500 万桶。

与此同时，特朗普周一延长了航运法《琼斯法案》的暂停期限，该法案限制美国港口与美国船只之间的货物运输。他将豁免范围缩小到运输某些能源资源的船只。

美国能源部周一公布的数据显示，美国战略石油储备的石油库存已降至 3 亿桶以下，降至四十多年来的最低水平。特朗普3月份下令释放1.72亿桶石油，以缓解伊朗战争造成的破坏。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
